results.title: Digital transformation with clinical alerts and personalized ...
results.content: KPIN’s adjusted successful booking rate was 53.68%, with an abandonment rate of 2.94% (IQR: 2.77–3.11%), aligning with patient survey results showing an 8.63 percentage point increase for positive sentiment. KPIN takes patient-submitted free text input and detects high-acuity cases as part of its clinical alert system (CAS); then it recommends booking options for timely and appropriate care as part of its clinical navigation system (CNS). KPIN integrates data (e.g., user age and gender) from multiple databases with the “Reason for Visit” input, to generate tailored clinical care offerings, which are safe and appropriate to book. A successful booking is defined as a patient completing the KPIN process and either (1) being offered at least one appointment option and the patient selects one, or (2) being presented with an alternative, appropriate care option—such as sending a message—through which the patient’s reason for visit can be addressed.
